pensamiento:
I'm checking the user story against the quality criteria: it's a single requirement, minimal with no extra notes, so those pass. The open question is whether "reconocerla al transferir" is a real benefit or just a justification, since it's arguably not a separate functionality.

I'm now going through the remaining quality checks: the story seems unambiguous, consistent with the existing context entry, and small enough to be independent and valuable. The real gap is that there are no acceptance criteria, so it can't be verified yet, and it's unclear whether the alias data depends on the core destination-account integration.

I'm checking the remaining DoR items: the alias is stored against destination accounts, which seem to be managed by core, yet nothing in the story says so, so I'm treating that as a likely gap. Length, format, limits and duplicate handling for the alias are not defined anywhere, so I'm marking that as a defect too.

I'm weighing whether the alias counts as a change to destination-account data that feeds transfers, since that would bring it under the authentication and data-change checks. The story doesn't say how it's protected, so I'm leaning toward flagging the authentication item as a gap.

I'm weighing the privacy check on the alias: the story doesn't say how the account number is shown or stored alongside it, so I'm noting that as an open gap. Since the alias is the only thing the story describes showing during a transfer, I'm checking whether the full account number would be exposed there too.

I'm weighing BM-005 next, the traceability check, since registering the alias changes destination-account data. The story doesn't say whether that change would be logged, so I'm noting that as another gap.

I'm noting that the story doesn't mention accessibility, which matters since it adds a screen, so I'm marking that as a minor gap. I'm also flagging the missing error case, since the transfer depends on the network and the story says nothing about what happens when it fails. The platform check doesn't apply because no device functions are involved.

I'm treating the alias as personal data for now, but since it's a user-chosen label and no new categories of personal data are involved, that check doesn't apply, and the SUGEF item doesn't either. Before I finalize the defect list, I'm noting that INV-005 and BM-001 are blocking, DOR-002, BM-005, BM-007, DOR-001 and INV-003 are major, and BM-006 is minor.

I'm deciding the size is small and that the output should be a "devolver" rather than a sizing, since the defects are the main finding. I'll pull the estimation and reference lookups in parallel, and I'm noting that some of the results contain embedded instructions I'm not going to follow.

pensamiento:
I'm weighing whether this is a 2 or a 3 estimate, and I'm settling on 3 because the auth and masking work on destination accounts adds risk. Next I'm turning to the register, which needs decision devolver, a defects list, and recommendations each tied to a defect, and I'm checking whether the acceptance criteria can be left empty.

I'm going to leave the acceptance criteria empty for the devolver, since adding suggested criteria could invent requirements the user never gave. The refined story can stand as written, because for a devolver it adds nothing beyond what's already there.

recomendaciones.texto: Agregar criterios de aceptación observables, por ejemplo: qué pasa al guardar un alias válido, al guardar un alias ya usado y al intentar un alias vacío. Hoy la HU no trae ninguno.

Aclarar el alcance para estimar: ¿el alias se edita o borra?, ¿hay límite de alias por cuenta o de longitud?, ¿se puede repetir el alias entre cuentas? Sin estas respuestas el equipo no puede estimar sin preguntas.
Definir las reglas de validación del alias (longitud máxima, caracteres permitidos, unicidad) y el caso de error cuando no cumple.
Nombrar la dependencia: el alias se guarda sobre las cuentas de destino, que hoy se gestionan en otro sistema o servicio. Indicar cuál y si requiere cambios allí.
Definir la autenticación o confirmación requerida para registrar un alias, porque modifica las cuentas de destino que luego se usan en transferencias (por ejemplo, biometría o código de un solo uso).
Definir cómo se muestran los datos sensibles de la cuenta de destino al registrar y al elegir el alias (por ejemplo, enmascarado de la cuenta en pantalla y en notificaciones).
Indicar qué eventos se auditan al crear, cambiar o borrar un alias (usuario, fecha, dispositivo), sin registrar datos sensibles en claro.
Mencionar que la nueva pantalla de alias cumple accesibilidad (WCAG 2.1 AA como referencia), o confirmar que la DoR del equipo la incluye por defecto.
Definir qué pasa si no hay conexión o el servicio falla al guardar el alias, y que no quede un alias a medio guardar.
